r0.why: Lithification defined as poorly consolidated sediment turning to sedimentary rock, placed in early stages of diagenesis [3]; diagenesis and its first causes [1].

r1.why: Compaction under successive layers and cementing by precipitated minerals [8]; porosity drop, water expulsion in clays, assemblages unaltered [3]; porosity usually falls except rare cases like dissolution [10].

r2.why: Excludes weathering and deep metamorphism [5], no sharp boundary but metamorphism at higher T and P [6], pressure and temperature matter only at much deeper burial [2].

r3.why: Replacement of grains, rock fragments and fossils by calcite, siderite, pyrite [9]; influential factors listed match [7].

r4.why: Buried organic molecules break down with rising temperature and pressure [25], first few hundred meters, kerogens and bitumens [26], hydrocarbons from thermal alteration of kerogens generally accepted [27].

r5.why: Geologic history and nature/type of circulating fluids [11]; commercial value for assessing mineral and hydrocarbon deposits [12].
